headline: Transaction growth picks up, but margins keep sliding
summary_short: Western Union's Q2 2026 revenue was $1,013.2 million, up 3.1% q/q but down 1.3% y/y, while net income fell 37.2% y/y to $76.7 million as higher agent commissions, compliance costs, and interest expense outweighed a pickup in transaction growth.
summary_long: Revenue fell 1% y/y to $1,013.2M as Consumer Money Transfer revenue dropped 2% on North America (lower US-outbound remittances amid immigration/macro headwinds) and Latin America softness, offset by 13% growth in Middle East/Africa/South Asia and a 25% jump in Branded Digital transactions; Consumer Services revenue rose 4% on travel-money and check-acceptance growth. Operating income fell 31% y/y to $132.1M on higher agent commissions, acquisition-related employee/real estate costs, and compliance costs; net income fell 37% to $76.7M, also hit by higher interest expense on the 2029 Notes. Western Union repurchased $53.7M of stock and paid $147.0M in dividends in H1. FY2026 guidance: 3-5% GAAP revenue growth, 4-6% adjusted revenue growth, $1.25-$1.35 adjusted EPS.
